- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to over-forecast; reduce forecast to match downward pressure.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1-2 days); cap forecast at 1-2% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
- In mean-reversion scenarios (sentiment neutral or mixed), model frequently lags; add 0.5–1.5% lagged adjustment to forecast to capture momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price volatility in high-sentiment periods; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for sentiment > 0.67.
- When sentiment shifts abruptly (e.g., from negative to positive), model reacts slowly; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment change.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 7-day low in high-sentiment periods — model tends to underestimate support levels.
